The note describes that PISA uses complex sampling and that technical standards include school participation and student response-rate targets; in Hong Kong (China), student response rates decreased and fell below the minimum target, and school participation also fell short. The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method, so the specific weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For analysts using the PISA database, the appropriate approach is to apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights (as documented in the PISA Reader’s Guide) when estimating means, shares, and uncertainty intervals.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Hong Kong (China) performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to 2018 and 2012. It reports mean performance trends, shares of students reaching proficiency levels (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and distributional gaps such as widening between the top and bottom deciles in mathematics and science from 2018 to 2022. The note also highlights subgroup patterns: socioeconomic status (ESCS) is associated with mathematics performance, boys outperform girls in mathematics while girls outperform boys in reading, and immigrant background shows differences that change after accounting for socioeconomic profile. Methodologically, the factsheet flags that Hong Kong (China) had student response rates below PISA technical minimums, implying potential (small) upward bias from non-response, and it advises caution for interpretation. The document is descriptive and does not provide ML model training, predictive metrics, or an explicit PV/missing-data procedure for this factsheet itself.
